title: RIFT: KV Cache Compression for Draft Models with Complementary Compressibility Training
summary: RIFT replaces static prefill-time KV cache selection in speculative drafters with periodic selection refreshes during decoding, plus a sparse-mask training phase that makes the drafter robust to a compressed cache. The costs are extra decode latency from refresh score calculations (partially mitigated by an adaptive refresh schedule) and the engineering and training burden of fine-tuning the drafter for compressibility. It can fail where acceptance-length gains do not offset refresh latency, where the adaptive schedule misjudges refresh timing on unfamiliar workloads, or where the reader lacks the pipeline to retrain and validate a drafter against their target model.
rationale: The method targets a real constraint (drafter KV memory in long-output speculative serving on a single GPU), but its benefit depends on the reader's acceptance-length profile and their ability to retrain a drafter, so it warrants a small-scale pilot rather than direct adoption.
technique: Refreshed KV cache selection for speculative drafters

claims.statement: RIFT replaces static prefill-time KV cache selection in speculative drafters with periodic selection refreshes during decoding, plus a sparse-mask training phase that makes the drafter robust to a compressed cache. The costs are extra decode latency from refresh score calculations (partially mitigated by an adaptive refresh schedule) and the engineering and training burden of fine-tuning the drafter for compressibility. It can fail where acceptance-length gains do not offset refresh latency, where the adaptive schedule misjudges refresh timing on unfamiliar workloads, or where the reader lacks the pipeline to retrain and validate a drafter against their target model.

RIFT with compressibility training retains over 98% of full-cache acceptance length on 32K-token inputs and 4K-token outputs while holding the drafter KV cache to an 8K-token budget (roughly a 4x reduction relative to the full context).
